representative_tasks.task: Warmup+cosine LambdaLR built over total_steps but stepped once per epoch; loss barely moves - is the scheduler placement correct?
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Says the schedule is in optimizer steps so scheduler.step() goes once per batch; explains that per-epoch stepping leaves the LR stuck in warmup at a few percent of the peak; suggests logging the LR

representative_tasks.task: Early stopping monitors training loss and keeps the final weights
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Monitors validation loss (per-sample mean), checkpoints on improvement, restores the best checkpoint after the loop, fails loudly on a non-finite validation loss

representative_tasks.task: Add mixed precision and gradient clipping to an existing loop
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: autocast + torch.amp.GradScaler on CUDA (disabled on CPU), scaler.unscale_ before clip_grad_norm_, bf16 noted as usually not needing a scaler

negative_cases: Gradient clipping applied to still-scaled fp16 gradients (clip before scaler.unscale_) (planned)
fp16 AMP producing NaN loss where the user proposes removing GradScaler (planned)
rubric: Scheduler stepping granularity matched to the units the schedule was built in, with the concrete consequence of a mismatch
Early stopping on a validation signal with best-checkpoint restore, not final weights
AMP ordering (unscale_ before clipping) and dtype trade-offs stated correctly when relevant
Heuristics (warmup fraction, patience, weight decay groups) phrased as defaults to validate, not universal rules
prerequisites: example-deps (torch, numpy) for executable tests; CPU only
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Executable tests need the example-test dependencies (see docs/EXAMPLE-TESTS.md) and run via run_evals.py --run-executable; they run CPU-only with AMP disabled, so the CUDA fp16 path is not exercised.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
expected_artifacts: best.pt holding the best-validation-loss model/optimizer state, restored into the model after early stopping
A warmup+cosine lr_lambda that reaches the peak after warmup and stays near zero past total_steps
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
Executable tests run CPU-only with AMP disabled; GradScaler/autocast on CUDA is not executed by anything in this repository.

The scheduler case's expected answer (per-epoch stepping of a per-step schedule leaves the LR stuck in warmup) was checked numerically in the example venv; the skill's own Gotcha wording describes this mismatch as compressing the decay, which is the effect of the opposite mismatch.

An independent reviewer's stress test (30 texts written after reading the patterns, so adversarial rather than blind; 23 wrong, 7 correct across all five skills of this workstream) initially had 16/23 wrong answers passing every hard assertion and 6/7 correct answers failing one. The patterns were then fixed and these texts kept verbatim as fail.adversarial* / pass.blind* fixtures, so the post-fix 30/30 is a regression result, not a held-out discrimination rate.
unsupported_use_cases: Searching hyperparameters such as LR or weight decay (hyperparameter-tuning)
